summary: SUNDARBAN SENTINEL is an integrated environmental monitoring and conservation initiative designed to protect the Sundarbans, the world’s largest contiguous mangrove forest. By combining satellite remote sensing, IoT sensor networks, and community-led patrolling, the project delivers real-time intelligence to track mangrove canopy health, coastal erosion, and illegal logging while deploying smart acoustic and camera traps to safeguard endangered wildlife like the Bengal tiger. Simultaneously, it monitors water salinity, rising sea levels, and cyclone impacts to power early-warning systems and equip forest rangers and local residents with mobile reporting tools. Ultimately, SUNDARBAN SENTINEL bridges advanced geospatial technology with grassroots stewardship to curb poaching, accelerate responses to ecological threats, and strengthen the long-term climate resilience of both the mangrove ecosystem and millions of vulnerable coastal residents.
details:
SUNDARBANS SENTINEL

An AI-Powered, Multi-Layer Environmental Intelligence and Early-Warning System

1. Project Overview

Sundarbans Sentinel is an integrated, three-layer environmental intelligence platform designed to protect the Sundarbans mangrove ecosystem and the millions of people whose livelihoods and safety depend on it.

By connecting orbital Earth observation, autonomous ground-based IoT sensors, and community-driven environmental reporting, the platform transforms fragmented environmental data into actionable intelligence for conservation authorities, forest rangers, researchers, and vulnerable coastal communities.

The system combines satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, real-time environmental telemetry, and localized early-warning communication to identify emerging ecological threats, monitor environmental changes, and support faster, evidence-based decision-making.

Its core mission is simple: turn environmental data into timely action to protect forests, wildlife, and coastal communities.

2. What It Does and How It Works

Sundarbans Sentinel operates through three interconnected layers that continuously exchange environmental information.

A. Orbital Macro-Observation — Space Layer

The Space Layer provides large-scale environmental monitoring by integrating satellite imagery and geospatial datasets from NASA, ESA, and other Earth-observation sources.

Primary data sources include:

  • Landsat 8 and 9 for long-term vegetation and land-cover monitoring.
  • Copernicus Sentinel-2 for multispectral vegetation and water analysis.
  • Copernicus Sentinel-1 SAR for monitoring surface changes and inundation under cloudy conditions.
  • NASA MODIS and VIIRS for thermal anomalies and fire detection.
  • Cyclone tracks and available meteorological datasets for coastal risk assessment.

Automated geospatial pipelines process available satellite observations to calculate environmental indicators, including the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), and Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI).

Machine learning and time-series analysis help identify:

  • Mangrove canopy degradation and vegetation stress.
  • Potential illegal clearing and land-cover changes.
  • Riverbank erosion and changing tidal channels.
  • Surface-water expansion and potential storm-surge inundation.
  • Environmental changes following major cyclones.

By combining optical imagery with Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), the platform maintains monitoring capabilities during periods of heavy cloud cover, particularly throughout the Bangladesh monsoon season.

Monitoring frequency depends on satellite revisit schedules, data availability, and processing latency.

B. Autonomous Ground Telemetry — IoT Layer

The IoT Layer complements satellite observations with localized environmental measurements from proposed solar-powered monitoring stations deployed at strategically selected riverbanks, forest edges, and vulnerable coastal locations.

Environmental monitoring capabilities include:

  • Water conductivity and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) as indicators of changing salinity.
  • Water pH for assessing changes in aquatic conditions.
  • Water-level and tidal-fluctuation monitoring.
  • Ambient acoustic monitoring for detecting unusual human and mechanical activity.

The proposed sensor stations use ESP32 microcontrollers to collect and process measurements locally.

Lightweight TinyML audio-classification models can analyze acoustic patterns directly on the device to identify sounds associated with chainsaws, motorized boats, and other potentially unauthorized activities.

Rather than transmitting continuous audio recordings, the system can send compact event notifications and sensor readings through low-power, long-range LoRa-based communication networks.

Strategically positioned gateways and relay nodes help extend communication coverage into remote areas where conventional cellular connectivity is unreliable.

C. Action, Simulation and Response — Community Layer

The Community Layer transforms satellite observations and ground-level sensor readings into practical conservation and disaster-response intelligence.

Information from both monitoring layers converges on the Sundarbans Sentinel Interactive Dashboard, providing users with:

  • Interactive satellite-based environmental maps.
  • AI-assisted anomaly detection and vegetation-health heatmaps.
  • Historical environmental trends and change analysis.
  • Salinity and tidal-monitoring indicators.
  • Cyclone and potential storm-surge impact simulations.
  • Geospatial alerts highlighting areas requiring investigation.

The platform is designed to support localized Bengali SMS and automated voice alerts for vulnerable communities.

It also provides offline-first mapping capabilities for forest rangers and Village Tiger Response Teams, helping field personnel access relevant information in areas with limited internet connectivity.

Community members, including honey collectors (Mawalis) and fishermen, can contribute through a voice-assisted and icon-driven reporting interface, allowing them to report environmental hazards and help validate remote-sensing observations.

3. Expected Benefits and Environmental Impact

A. Faster Threat Detection and Response

Combining satellite-based anomaly detection with local acoustic monitoring can help identify suspicious activities earlier than conventional periodic patrols alone.

The platform helps forest authorities prioritize potentially affected locations and coordinate targeted field investigations, reducing the time and resources required to identify emerging threats.

B. Improved Cyclone and Salinity Resilience

By combining satellite observations, water-quality measurements, tidal monitoring, and cyclone information, Sundarbans Sentinel supports a better understanding of coastal environmental risks.

Its intended capabilities include identifying areas vulnerable to storm-surge inundation, tracking changing salinity patterns, and communicating localized warnings that help farmers, fishermen, and coastal households prepare for environmental threats.

C. Human-Wildlife Conflict Awareness

Habitat degradation and changing environmental conditions can increase pressure along forest-community boundaries.

By mapping habitat changes, incorporating verified community sightings, and identifying environmentally vulnerable locations, the platform can help authorities prioritize human-wildlife conflict monitoring.

Sensitive wildlife-location data remains restricted to authorized conservation personnel.

D. Evidence-Based Conservation and Climate Policy

The platform creates a longitudinal environmental dataset that can help researchers and policymakers assess:

  • Mangrove vegetation trends and recovery patterns.
  • Coastal erosion and land-cover changes.
  • Environmental impacts following cyclones.
  • Habitat conditions and ecosystem degradation.
  • Potential mangrove blue-carbon conservation opportunities.

These insights can contribute to evidence-based conservation planning, climate adaptation strategies, and future blue-carbon assessments.

4. Technology Stack and Implementation Architecture

Programming Languages

  • Python: Geospatial processing, satellite-data pipelines, backend services, and machine learning.
  • TypeScript / JavaScript: Interactive web dashboard, frontend interfaces, and geospatial visualization.
  • C / C++: Embedded firmware and IoT sensor integration.

Geospatial Data Processing and Visualization

  • Google Earth Engine API.
  • QGIS.
  • GDAL.
  • Mapbox GL JS.
  • Leaflet.
  • PostGIS.

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

  • PyTorch / TensorFlow for geospatial analysis and environmental anomaly detection.
  • TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers for edge inference.
  • Edge Impulse for lightweight acoustic classification.
  • Time-series analysis for detecting long-term environmental changes.

Backend and Cloud Infrastructure

  • FastAPI for backend APIs.
  • PostgreSQL with PostGIS for geospatial data management.
  • Docker for deployment and service management.
  • Firebase and/or SMS and voice communication services for alert delivery.

Proposed Hardware Architecture

  • ESP32 microcontrollers.
  • SX1276 LoRa radio transceivers.
  • Industrial electrical-conductivity/TDS and pH sensors.
  • Non-contact ultrasonic water-level sensors.
  • Acoustic monitoring modules.
  • Solar charging systems with LiFePO4 battery storage.
  • IP68-rated marine-grade enclosures and protective conformal coatings.

5. What Makes Sundarbans Sentinel Innovative?

A. All-Weather Environmental Intelligence

Traditional optical satellite imagery is frequently affected by cloud cover, especially during the Bangladesh monsoon season.

Sundarbans Sentinel addresses this limitation by combining optical observations from Landsat and Sentinel-2 with cloud-penetrating Sentinel-1 SAR data.

This multi-sensor approach enables environmental monitoring to continue when conventional optical imagery becomes unavailable, providing a more consistent picture of changing forest and coastal conditions.

B. Connectivity-Independent Ground Monitoring

Large portions of the Sundarbans consist of remote waterways and dense mangrove forests where cellular connectivity is limited.

The platform proposes low-power LoRa-based communication supported by strategically deployed gateways and relay nodes.

By processing sensor data locally and transmitting lightweight alerts instead of continuous raw data, the system reduces communication requirements and supports monitoring in remote locations.

C. Edge AI for Immediate Environmental Threat Detection

Instead of depending entirely on centralized cloud-based analysis, Sundarbans Sentinel brings selected machine learning capabilities directly to ESP32-based monitoring devices.

This enables local classification of suspicious acoustic patterns and environmental events, allowing preliminary alerts to be generated even when internet access is unavailable.

D. Two-Way Community-Based Environmental Intelligence

The platform does not treat coastal communities as passive recipients of environmental warnings.

Through voice-assisted reporting and accessible visual interfaces, local fishermen, honey collectors, and other community members can contribute environmental observations.

This creates a two-way information network in which satellite and sensor observations can be supplemented and validated through local knowledge.

6. Critical Design Considerations

A. Marine Durability and Environmental Protection

High salinity, humidity, sediment, and tidal submergence can damage conventional electronic equipment.

The proposed hardware uses marine-grade protective enclosures, conformal coatings, corrosion-resistant components, and non-contact ultrasonic water-level sensors where appropriate.

Equipment placement and maintenance schedules must account for tidal conditions, biofouling, and accessibility.

B. Energy Efficiency and Autonomous Operation

Replacing batteries and maintaining equipment in remote, wildlife-sensitive locations can be challenging.

The IoT architecture therefore prioritizes solar-assisted power, intelligent deep-sleep duty cycles, energy-efficient sensor sampling, and lightweight edge-AI models.

Power budgets must be validated against actual solar exposure, canopy shading, weather conditions, and seasonal energy requirements.

C. Accessibility and Community Inclusion

Environmental intelligence is useful only when people can understand and act on it.

The platform prioritizes Bengali-language voice alerts, basic SMS notifications, icon-driven interfaces, and offline mapping to accommodate users with different levels of digital literacy and connectivity.

D. Data Security and Wildlife Protection

Sensitive ecological information must not become a tool for illegal exploitation.

The platform therefore proposes role-based access control, encrypted communications, and restricted access to precise wildlife coordinates and sensitive ranger patrol information.

Public-facing environmental maps can provide aggregated or generalized information without exposing vulnerable wildlife locations.

7. Long-Term Vision

Sundarbans Sentinel aims to evolve into a scalable environmental intelligence framework that connects space-based observation, autonomous ground monitoring, artificial intelligence, and community participation.

Although initially designed around the Bangladesh Sundarbans, its modular architecture could eventually be adapted to other mangrove ecosystems, coastal wetlands, and climate-vulnerable regions around the world.

By combining scientific observation with local knowledge and actionable intelligence, Sundarbans Sentinel seeks to strengthen ecosystem resilience, improve conservation response, and help safeguard communities living on the frontlines of climate change.

Sundarbans Sentinel — From Space to Shore, Turning Environmental Intelligence into Action.
